highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.152.0 introduces Graphite GPU backend bindings, async ReadPixels, and multiple memory-safety fixes.
highlights_body: Skia's next-generation Graphite rendering pipeline is now accessible from .NET via new Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn bindings. A backend-neutral async ReadPixels API rounds out the GPU surface additions. Two native use-after-free bugs are fixed, and a new SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET package eases Vulkan context setup. Multiple performance improvements reduce allocations and P/Invoke overhead.

bullets.lead: Skia updated to Chrome milestone m152
bullets.detail: The Skia engine is updated to the Chrome m152 milestone, bringing upstream rendering improvements and bug fixes from Google.

bullets.lead: Upstream m151 and m152 stability fixes applied
bullets.detail: Several upstream cherry-pick syncs from the Skia chrome/m151 and m152 branches apply engine stability and correctness improvements.

bullets.lead: Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn
bullets.detail: New bindings expose Skia's next-generation Graphite rendering pipeline. Consumers can create Graphite GPU contexts for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn backends, unlocking the modern, lower-overhead GPU path.

bullets.lead: Backend-neutral async RequestReadPixels on SKImage and SKSurface
bullets.detail: A new async ReadPixels API lets callers read pixel data from GPU-backed images and surfaces without blocking the render thread, working across all supported GPU backends.

A dedicated NuGet package wraps the Silk.NET Vulkan interop layer, making it straightforward to wire up Vulkan contexts without custom P/Invoke boilerplate. Vulkan tests now run on Android and Linux CI.
All .sln solution files are converted to the modern .slnx format, aligning with current .NET SDK tooling.
The SKRegion source was not kept alive during SpanIterator iteration, allowing the GC to collect it mid-use and cause native crashes. The region is now rooted for the lifetime of the iterator.

bullets.lead: Native use-after-free in SKPixmap.ExtractSubset and With* fixed
bullets.detail: SKPixmap wrappers that borrow pixel memory from a parent object did not keep that parent alive, risking native crashes after GC. The parent pixel source is now rooted for the lifetime of the derived pixmap.

bullets.lead: CoTaskMem pixel-buffer leak in SKImage.Create fixed
bullets.detail: A pixel buffer allocated during raster image creation was not freed when the native call failed, producing a silent native memory leak. The buffer is now correctly released on failure.

HandleDictionary's reflection check is now cached instead of repeated on every registration call. SKData.SaveTo avoids a double buffer copy. GetEncodedText eliminates an intermediate string allocation. SKRuntimeEffectUniforms pre-sizes its lookup map. Together these reduce GC pressure in common hot paths.

bullets.lead: FreeType font rendering on Windows Nano Server
bullets.detail: Nano Server environments lack the GDI font stack. SkiaSharp now falls back to FreeType on Nano Server, enabling text rendering in containerised Windows workloads that was previously broken.

bullets.lead: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, and Nano Server containerized test legs added
bullets.detail: Containerised CI test legs for Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Nano Server ensure SkiaSharp is continuously validated across these production-relevant environments.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: Implemented FreeType font support for Windows Nano Server, unblocking text rendering in GDI-less container environments.
contributor_summaries.mmitche: Improved the Windows native build by initializing the MSVC environment once per build rather than per invocation.
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Authored the Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn.
